metadata.title: OrbitStreet — Earth System Trend Detective
metadata.description: Is your corner of the planet really changing? Investigate real NASA POWER data: what is changing, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant.

hero.title: Is your corner of the planet really changing?
hero.subtitle: OrbitStreet turns anyone into an Earth System Trend Detective. Pick any place and a variable — temperature, rainfall, humidity — and find out what is changing, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant.

map.headline: NASA's grid cell measures ~50 km; your street doesn't.
map.description: Spin the planet, zoom in with the magnifiers and click anywhere on the globe to pick a point. Then choose a variable and query real NASA POWER data for that place.
map.dragHint: Drag to rotate · Click + wheel to zoom · Click to pick a point
map.ariaGlobe: Interactive 3D globe: drag to rotate the continents and click to pick precise coordinates
map.scrollCue: Scroll to see the four questions
map.variablesSubtitle: Choose which variable to analyze in the cell
map.yearsNoteImpractical: Local sensor: not viable in a lifetime
map.yearsNoteWhy: Why? A ground node installed here today would take those years to confirm the trend on its own: it measures when your street starts producing evidence.
map.previewNote: The analysis runs right here with the same deterministic engine (Mann-Kendall + Sen) as Detective Mode; never invented data.

questions.title: Every good detective asks four questions
questions.subtitle: OrbitStreet answers all of them with decades of real NASA data and mathematics — never guesses.

what.title: What is changing?
what.description: Temperature highs, days above 35 °C, rainfall, humidity: real variables measured by NASA Earth science missions and models.

where.title: Where is it changing?
where.description: Any place on Earth you choose — your city, your region — at NASA grid-cell scale, and later at street level with our open-hardware node.

howMuch.title: How much is it changing?
howMuch.description: The rate of change in real units, such as °C per decade, with confidence intervals — not just a line going up.

significant.title: Is it significant?
significant.description: A rising line may be just natural noise. We apply the same statistical tests scientists use (Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope) before calling a change real.

honesty.title: Honest by design
honesty.subtitle: We would rather answer a few questions well than promise what the data cannot support.

reanalysis.title: We say what the data is
reanalysis.description: NASA POWER is a reanalysis (MERRA-2), not a direct satellite measurement. We state that clearly, as any honest tool should.

deterministic.title: Statistics, not improvisation
deterministic.description: Every number is computed deterministically in code. AI only writes the plain-language report; it never calculates figures.

yearsNeeded.title: A new sensor proves nothing
yearsNeeded.description: A few weeks of local data cannot reveal a climate trend. Instead, we tell you how many years of measurements would be needed.

simulated.title: No fake data in disguise
simulated.description: Any simulated or test data is always clearly labeled [SIMULATED DATA / TESTBED].

detective.title: Detective Mode
detective.subtitle: Pick a place and an Earth variable. OrbitStreet downloads decades of real NASA data, runs the statistical tests for you and answers the four detective questions. The URL is shareable: send your investigation to anyone.

form.customHint: Coordinates are only used when “Custom” is selected as the place. Data starts in 1981.

T2M.label: Average air temperature (2 m)
T2M.description: Daily average air temperature at 2 meters above the ground, from the MERRA-2 reanalysis.

T2M_MAX.label: Maximum temperature
T2M_MAX.description: The highest temperature of each day. Ideal for studying heat waves and extreme heat.

T2M_MIN.label: Minimum temperature
T2M_MIN.description: The lowest temperature of each day.

RH2M.label: Relative humidity (2 m)
RH2M.description: The amount of water vapor in the air, as a percentage.

PRECTOTCORR.label: Total precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.description: Accumulated rainfall, analyzed as the annual total (mm per year).

PS.label: Surface pressure
PS.description: The atmospheric pressure at ground level.

DAYS_ABOVE_THRESHOLD.label: Days above 35 °C
DAYS_ABOVE_THRESHOLD.description: Number of days per year whose maximum temperature exceeded 35 °C: a direct measure of extreme heat.

results.title: Investigation results
results.whereNote: NASA grid cell (~50 km): your street may differ — that is exactly the role of the ground node.
results.yearsNeededTitle: How long would a local sensor need?
results.yearsNeededBody: With the natural variability of this series, a new sensor in this location would need about {years} years of measurements before this trend becomes statistically detectable. Starting to measure today is exactly how those years get counted.
results.yearsNeededInfinite: This series is too noisy or too flat to estimate a horizon. Honestly, no promise is made here.
results.yearsNeededHuge: Natural variability outweighs the signal by orders of magnitude: a local sensor here wouldn't confirm this trend even in a thousand years. Honestly, from the ground it is practically undetectable — here the satellite cell is the only viable tool.
results.yearsNeededWhy: Why does this number matter? It tells you with data whether a citizen node on this block can produce evidence within a human timescale, or whether only the satellite cell — with decades of history — can see this trend. This figure is for a SINGLE sensor: a network of N independent nodes shortens it ≈ N-fold, because uncertainty averages down with the square root of N.
results.ciCrossesZero: The interval crosses zero: uncertain magnitude
results.ciSameSign: The whole interval keeps the same sign
results.alphaNote: Above the α = 0.05 threshold of the Mann-Kendall test
results.validResultNote: Valid result: natural variability explains this swing

glossary.title: Learn to read these results
glossary.pValue: p-value: the probability of getting a trend like this by pure chance. Below 0.05, scientists accept the trend as statistically significant.
glossary.senSlope: Sen's slope: a robust estimate of the rate of change, unaffected by a few extreme years. It is expressed in real units per decade.
glossary.confidenceInterval: Confidence interval: the range where the true slope most likely lies. If it includes zero, the direction of the change is not yet certain.

report.title: Detective report
report.badgeGemini: Written by Gemini · numbers computed deterministically
report.badgeTemplate: Automatic local summary · AI not configured
report.aiDisclaimer: The AI only writes the narrative: every number was computed by deterministic code, never by the model.
report.templateDisclaimer: This summary is generated locally from the computed results.
report.error: The report could not be generated. The numbers above remain valid.
report.s2: Sen's slope: {slope} per decade (95% confidence interval: {low} to {high}).
report.verdictYes: The trend is statistically significant: this change is very unlikely to be random noise.
report.verdictNo: The trend does not yet reach statistical significance — sometimes a trend simply needs more years of data to be confirmed.
report.yearsNote: With this natural variability, a new local sensor would need about {years} years of measurements to confirm this trend.

account.title: Your detective account
account.subtitle: Investigating NASA data is open to everyone. An account is only needed to upload your own measurements and save your progress — it protects the community data from bots.
account.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Stored only as a scrypt hash, never in clear text.
account.cooldownNote: You can upload one series every {minutes} minutes.
account.privacyNote: We only store your email, display name and password hash. Nothing else. No trackers.

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.email_taken: That email is already registered. Try logging in.
errors.weak_password: Password must be at least 8 characters long.
errors.invalid_name: Display name must be 1 to 40 characters.

upload.title: Upload your series
upload.subtitle: Contribute your own measurements — a homemade rain gauge, a school thermometer, a personal weather station. Your series runs through the exact same deterministic statistics as NASA data, and is always labeled as community data (unvalidated).
upload.loginRequired: Uploading data requires an account with a password. This protects the community database from bots and mass uploads.
upload.dataHint: One line per day: YYYY-MM-DD,value — or paste a JSON array [{"date": "…", "value": …}].
upload.resultEmpty: Upload a series to see its analysis here: Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope with 95% confidence interval, and the honest verdict.
upload.yearsNeededBody: With this variability, about {years} years of measurements would be needed to confirm a trend with statistical confidence. Keep measuring!
upload.yearsNeededInfinite: This series is too short or noisy to estimate a time horizon. That is honest, not a failure.
upload.yearsNeededHuge: This series' variability outweighs the signal: a local sensor wouldn't confirm the trend even in a thousand years. That is honest, not a failure.
upload.communityLabel: Community data, unvalidated — never mixed with NASA data without its label.
